entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9856"/><div sID="gen17472" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9856"/><hi type="bold">15. my beloved--</hi>My elect people, Judea; this aggravates their ingratitude (<reference osisRef="Jer.12.7">Jr 12:7</reference>).<div eID="gen17472" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17473" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">lewdness with many--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Ezek.16.25">Eze 16:25</reference>). Rather, "that great (or, manifold) enormity"; literally, "the enormity, the manifold"; namely, their idolatry, which made their worship of God in the temple a mockery (compare <reference osisRef="Jer.7.10">Jr 7:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.23.39">Eze 23:39</reference>) [Henderson].<div eID="gen17473" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17474" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">holy flesh--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Hag.2.12-Hag.2.14">Hag 2:12-14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Titus.1.15">Tit 1:15</reference>), namely, the sacrifices, which, through the guilt of the Jews, were no longer holy, that is, acceptable to God. The sacrifices on which they relied will, therefore, no longer protect them. Judah is represented as a priest's wife, who, by adultery, has forfeited her share in the flesh of the sacrifices, and yet boasts of her prerogative at the very same time [Horsley].<div eID="gen17474" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17475" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">when thou doest evil--</hi>literally, "when thy evil" (is at hand). Piscator translates, "When thy calamity is at hand (according to God's threats), thou gloriest" (against God, instead of humbling thyself). English Version is best (compare <reference osisRef="Prov.2.14">Pr 2:14</reference>). <div eID="gen17475" type="x-p"/>
